1. The halo effect: people judge your intelligence, your work and your personality by how you look. It shows up in job interviews, business deals, your relationship and online dating.
2. You get more done: if you don't spend the time in the gym, you'll spend it in the doctor's office.
3. Better mental health: your body and your mind go hand in hand.
4. Bad health is ludicrously expensive: diabetes, ambulance rides, amputations and eye injections cost far more than taking care of yourself now.

Money does you no good if you're dead, or if you're sick.

This is part 1 of 3. Part 2, what to cut to afford getting in shape, comes out next. Part 3 covers what to buy for your health at every income level.
